title: Xpert Ultra and molecular WRDs
dek: WHO-recommended rapid diagnostics are the front door: MTBC DNA plus an rpoB window. Ultra added IS6110/IS1081 and melt — and the trace call that needs a brain.
story: WHO’s diagnostic spine starts with a WHO-recommended rapid molecular diagnostic (mWRD) on an appropriate specimen — not smear-first, not IGRA-first. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra is the most widely deployed: it detects MTBC DNA and interrogates the rpoB RRDR as a rifampin surrogate in the same cartridge.

Ultra lowered the limit of detection versus classic Xpert by adding multi-copy IS6110 and IS1081 targets and melt analysis. The cost is the “trace” semi-quantitative band: true paucibacillary disease, or lingering DNA, especially in previously treated lungs. Trace often makes RIF indeterminate because the RRDR probes starved for template.

Cousins: Truenat MTB/RIF, TB-LAMP (no RIF), line-probe assays, and targeted NGS as follow-on WRDs. A WRD is defined by WHO evaluation, not by the marketing word “PCR.” None of them is WGS, and none grades BDQ/LZD/Pa by itself.
deepTitle: Failure modes a lab should recite
deep: Silent RRDR SNPs can drop a probe and look RIF-R. Disputed/borderline rpoB alleles can look RIF-R on cartridge and fussy on MGIT. I491F is outside the window and looks RIF-S on Xpert.
Heteroresistance below the probe’s mixing threshold looks RIF-S. That is not a reason to skip culture.
Stool as a pediatric WRD specimen is a 2020s WHO recommendation: you are detecting swallowed DNA/bacilli, not inventing a new disease site.
False MTB-not-detected in a high-suspicion HIV or pediatric case is an expected sensitivity miss. Repeat, change specimen, culture, LAM — do not stop.

visual.caption: What Ultra actually looks at: multi-copy IS elements for detection sensitivity, plus the rpoB RRDR for rifampin. Trace can light IS without a callable RRDR.

example.title: Trace, RIF indeterminate, prior TB
example.setup: Treated two years ago, chronic cough, scarred CXR, Ultra trace / RIF indeterminate, smear negative.

steps.title: Name the missing result
steps.body: You do not have a rifampin call. Do not write RIF-S.

steps.title: Viability
steps.body: Culture and a fresh specimen. Trace in retreatment is the relic-DNA trap.

steps.title: If disease is likely, treat as TB with unknown RIF pending
steps.body: Clinical judgement plus follow-on tNGS/WGS if available — not “trace equals colonisation” by slogan.

example.takeaway: Ultra is a windowed NAAT. Trace is a band, not a DST.

check.prompt: WHO’s preferred initial diagnostic test for TB disease in most settings is:
choices: A WHO-recommended rapid molecular diagnostic on an appropriate specimen
Chest radiograph alone as microbiologic proof
check.answer: A WHO-recommended rapid molecular diagnostic on an appropriate specimen
check.why: Smear is adjunctive; IGRA is not a disease test.

check.prompt: Ultra “trace” with RIF indeterminate most nearly means:
choices: Lowest positivity band, often IS-element driven; RRDR may lack template so RIF is uncalled
check.answer: Lowest positivity band, often IS-element driven; RRDR may lack template so RIF is uncalled

whyWrong.High-burden RR-TB is proven: Trace is the opposite of high.

check.prompt: On the Ultra track, why is I491F drawn to the right of the RRDR box?
choices: Because Ultra’s rpoB beacons do not tile codon 491
Because I491F is an IS6110 insertion
Because trace is defined at codon 491
Because I491F is a host SNP
check.answer: Because Ultra’s rpoB beacons do not tile codon 491
check.why: Same lesson as the rifampin plate, now in cartridge geometry.
check.figureHint: RRDR box ends before the I491F mark.
